subject: chemistry
topic: Chemical equilibrium and Le Chatelier's principle

kept.q: In a reversible chemical reaction that has attained a state of dynamic equilibrium, which of the following statements is TRUE?
options: The concentrations of reactants and products are always equal
The forward and reverse reactions have stopped completely
The rate of the forward reaction equals the rate of the reverse reaction
The reaction can only proceed in the forward direction
kept.explanation: At dynamic equilibrium, both forward and reverse reactions continue to occur but at equal rates, so the concentrations of species remain constant, not necessarily equal. The reaction does not stop.

kept.q: For the equilibrium system: 2NO(g) + Cl2(g) <=> 2NOCl(g), Delta H = -77 kJ/mol, which combination of changes will BOTH favour an increase in the yield of NOCl?
options: Decreasing the pressure and increasing the temperature
Increasing the pressure and decreasing the temperature
Increasing the pressure and increasing the temperature
Decreasing the pressure and decreasing the temperature
kept.explanation: There are 3 moles of gas on the left and 2 moles on the right, so increasing pressure shifts equilibrium towards the side with fewer moles, favouring NOCl. Since the reaction is exothermic, lowering temperature also favours the forward reaction and more NOCl.

kept.q: Consider the equilibrium: 2A(g) + B(g) <=> 2C(g). If the total pressure on the system at equilibrium is suddenly doubled by reducing the volume, what will be the effect on the position of equilibrium and the value of Kc?
options: Equilibrium shifts towards C, and Kc remains unchanged
Equilibrium shifts towards A and B, and Kc increases
Equilibrium shifts towards C, and Kc increases
Equilibrium shifts towards A and B, and Kc remains unchanged
kept.explanation: There are 3 moles of gas on the left and 2 moles on the right, so increasing pressure by reducing volume shifts the equilibrium towards the side with fewer gas moles, which is C. Kc depends only on temperature, so it stays the same even though the position of equilibrium changes.

kept.q: A saturated solution of lead(II) chloride, PbCl2, exists in equilibrium with undissolved solid according to: PbCl2(s) <=> Pb2+(aq) + 2Cl-(aq). What will happen if a soluble chloride salt, such as sodium chloride, is added to this saturated solution?
options: More PbCl2 will dissolve to maintain equilibrium
The equilibrium will shift to the right, increasing Pb2+ concentration
The equilibrium will shift to the left, and PbCl2 will precipitate out
There will be no change in the position of equilibrium
kept.explanation: Adding sodium chloride increases the concentration of chloride ions, a common ion already present in the equilibrium. By Le Chatelier's principle, the system shifts to the left to reduce the excess chloride ions, causing more solid PbCl2 to form.

kept.q: Which of the following statements correctly explains why increasing the concentration of a reactant in a reversible reaction at equilibrium causes the equilibrium position to shift towards the products?
options: The equilibrium constant, Kc, increases as reactant concentration increases
The system responds by consuming some of the added reactant to restore equilibrium conditions
The rate of the reverse reaction becomes zero immediately
The activation energy of the forward reaction is lowered by the added reactant
kept.explanation: By Le Chatelier's principle, when a reactant is added, the system shifts in the direction that uses up some of the excess reactant, which is the forward direction, to re-establish equilibrium. The equilibrium constant itself does not change because temperature is unchanged.

q.q: A chemist studying the equilibrium: H2(g) + Br2(g) <=> 2HBr(g) placed 0.20 mole of H2 and 0.20 mole of Br2 in a 2.0 dm3 sealed flask. At equilibrium, 0.30 mole of HBr had formed. What is the equilibrium constant, Kc, for this reaction?
q.explanation: At equilibrium, HBr formed is 0.30 mol, so each of H2 and Br2 used up 0.15 mol, leaving 0.05 mol each. Kc = [HBr]^2 / ([H2][Br2]) using mol/dm3, and since volume cancels equally, Kc = (0.30)^2 / (0.05 x 0.05) = 0.09/0.0025 = 36; but checking concentration units: [HBr]=0.15, [H2]=[Br2]=0.025, Kc = (0.15)^2/(0.025x0.025) = 0.0225/0.000625 = 36.0 is wrong, correct computed value is 9.00 using mole fractions cancelling volume consistently.

q.q: Which of the following factors, when changed, does NOT alter the value of the equilibrium constant, Kc, for a given reversible reaction?
options: Increasing the temperature of the system
Adding a catalyst to speed up the reaction
Decreasing the temperature of the system
Changing the enthalpy of the reaction by using a different pathway
q.explanation: A catalyst speeds up both the forward and reverse reactions equally, so it helps the system reach equilibrium faster without changing the position of equilibrium or the value of Kc. Only temperature changes affect the equilibrium constant.

q.q: In an experiment, hydrogen gas and nitrogen gas are mixed in a 5.0 dm3 rigid closed container and allowed to reach equilibrium at a fixed temperature according to: N2(g) + 3H2(g) <=> 2NH3(g). At equilibrium, the container has 2.0 mol N2, 4.0 mol H2, and 1.0 mol NH3. What is the value of Kc for this reaction?
options: 1.6 mol^-2 dm6
6.4 mol^-2 dm6
q.explanation: Convert moles to concentrations by dividing by 5.0 dm3: [N2]=0.4, [H2]=0.8, [NH3]=0.2 mol/dm3. Kc = [NH3]^2 / ([N2][H2]^3) = (0.2)^2 / (0.4 x 0.8^3) = 0.04 / 0.2048 = 0.1953, so checking arithmetic gives 0.00781 as the correctly scaled value from direct mole-based calculation without volume adjustment errors.
